h.select_rule: Keep hypotheses you rate at least 55% likely true but expect other models to rate below 50%, and name the specific naive reasoning that would mislead them. Drop anything you rate below 50% yourself, and anything obvious from structure alone. Keep fields and directions diverse.
h.strategy: Propose a broad, varied set of conditional hypotheses covering many different edited fields, conditioning fields and both directions. For each, briefly note your own probability that it holds and how an intuitive reader would judge it.

hyps.why: Upgrading conv1x1 to conv3x3 is an incremental gain, smaller than upgrading from none, skip or pool.
Diminishing returns: a conv3x3 already feeds the output directly, so another one adds less.
Diminishing returns when another conv3x3 already feeds the output node.
Adding a direct skip to the output where there was none improves gradient flow far more than swapping one op for another.
Filling an empty edge into the output gives a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
The conv1x1 to conv3x3 upgrade is smaller than the average upgrade into conv3x3.
Swapping a conv3x3 for a pool on the direct edge to the output loses more than swapping a weak op.
Replacing the first conv3x3 with a pool loses more than replacing a weaker op.
Replacing a missing direct edge with conv3x3 gives a large gain compared with replacing an existing op.
Dropping a conv3x3 into the output hurts more than dropping a weaker op.
